title: Concepts and terms in mech interp

cues.en: A big part of entering a new field is becoming familiar with the terminology that is used in that field,
cues.zh: 進新領域，很重要的是熟悉術語，

cues.en: and the concepts that are relevant for navigating in that research.
cues.zh: 以及研究中相關概念。

cues.en: I'm mostly going to be introducing concepts and terms in the next several sections as I introduce you to specific analyses and go through the Python demos and so on.
cues.zh: 接下來幾章，大多會隨分析、Python 示範，逐步介紹。

cues.en: But in this video, I do want to introduce you to a couple of concepts that will be useful to know before
cues.zh: 但這支先介紹幾個開始前

cues.en: getting started, and that are simple enough to understand conceptually, even without getting into the specifics of the analyses.
cues.zh: 值得知道、也不需分析細節就能理解的概念。

cues.en: The first concept, or actually this is more like a distinction of types of experimental approaches,
cues.zh: 第一，比較像實驗方法的區分，

cues.en: is the distinction between non-causal, sometimes called observation based and causal, which is also sometimes called intervention based mech interp research.
cues.zh: 非因果、也稱觀察式，與因果、也稱介入式機制研究。

cues.en: You can also think of this as correlational versus causational.
cues.zh: 也就是相關與因果。

cues.en: So the idea of non-causal or observation based research is just to push tokens through the model and
cues.zh: 非因果或觀察式，是把詞元送過模型，

cues.en: observe what happens to the activations and measure the weights and so on.
cues.zh: 觀察啟用、量測權重等等。

cues.en: You're not actually changing anything or manipulating anything in the model.
cues.zh: 不改變、操弄模型，

cues.en: You're just measuring what the model is naturally doing.
cues.zh: 只是測量自然行為。

cues.en: So the word hook here is a specific term used to inject a function into the model that will output the
cues.zh: hook 是特定術語，把函數插進模型，輸出

cues.en: activation values as they are being calculated.
cues.zh: 計算中的啟用值。

cues.en: You will learn how to create and implant hooks later on in the course.
cues.zh: 後面會學建立與植入。

cues.en: Causal approaches or intervention based approaches involve actually going in and manipulating or changing the activation values while the model is processing tokens.
cues.zh: 因果、介入式，則在處理詞元時，實際改變啟用值。

cues.en: As you might guess, the Non-causal method provides correlational evidence while the causal method provides causal evidence.
cues.zh: 非因果提供相關證據，因果提供因果證據。

cues.en: Now, you might be wondering why anyone would go for correlational evidence when it's possible to do causal manipulations.
cues.zh: 既能因果操弄，為何還做相關？

cues.en: The answer, which you will experience over the rest of this course, is that this kind of research
cues.zh: 後面會體驗，因為研究

cues.en: is just really difficult, in part because there are so many moving pieces inside a model.
cues.zh: 很難，內部環節太多。

cues.en: There are so many things you can manipulate in so many different ways that it becomes really daunting very quickly.
cues.zh: 太多東西、太多操弄方式，很快就令人卻步。

cues.en: So it's always a good idea, not just in MacIntyre, but in any branch of science to start with observations
cues.zh: 所以不只這領域，任何科學，最好從觀察開始，

cues.en: and then build hypotheses and theories and then start to look for causal evidence.
cues.zh: 建立假說、理論，再找因果證據。

cues.en: Relatedly, observation based methods can be based on empirical explorations, data mining with models
cues.zh: 觀察可以基於實證探索、模型資料探勘，

cues.en: and data, or maybe just random hunches that you might have, or curiosities that you might have and start coding on a rainy Sunday afternoon.
cues.zh: 或某個猜想、好奇，下雨的週日下午就開始寫程式。

cues.en: Of course, observation based research can also be based on very strong theoretical principles, but
cues.zh: 當然，也能基於強理論，

cues.en: the thing is that there isn't really a whole lot of really great theories at this point in mech interp just because it's such a new field.
cues.zh: 只是領域很新，還沒很多好理論。

cues.en: On the other hand, causal interventions technically can be done just by messing around and trying out a bunch of random things.
cues.zh: 介入技術上也能隨機亂試，

cues.en: But as I mentioned a moment ago, there are just so many possibilities for manipulations that this kind
cues.zh: 但選擇太多，

cues.en: of research is best done when you already have an idea of what to look for and what to test for.
cues.zh: 最好先知道要找、要測什麼。

cues.en: Ah yeah, these two points I've basically already explained, and for all of these reasons, it is still
cues.zh: 這兩點已解釋；因此仍然

cues.en: quite challenging because it involves a lot of linear algebra, statistics and coding.
cues.zh: 很有挑戰，涉及很多線代、統計、程式。

cues.en: But in my opinion, it's always best to start with observations.
cues.zh: 我認為最好先觀察，

cues.en: And then once you have a solid observation, you then move to causal intervention to test whether your observation is really part of a core mechanism.
cues.zh: 有扎實結果，再介入，測是否真屬核心機制。

cues.en: Anyway, I'm sure you've seen this course outline, so you know that there are different sections of the course for causal versus non causal approaches.
cues.zh: 你看過課綱，知道因果、非因果有不同章節。

cues.en: The next topic I'll introduce here is about interpreting trained models versus training interpretable models.
cues.zh: 接著區分：解釋訓練好的模型，與訓練可解釋模型。

cues.en: Now what does that what does that mean.
cues.zh: 什麼意思？

cues.en: What do these phrases mean.
cues.zh: 這些詞是什麼？

cues.en: Well to interpret trained models means that the models are trained without any regard to subsequent interpretability.
cues.zh: 前者，是訓練時不考慮後續可解釋性，

cues.en: Ability.
cues.zh: 也就是可解釋的程度。

cues.en: Instead, the models are trained to be as capable and useful as possible.
cues.zh: 只追求能力、實用。

cues.en: And then mcinturff happens after the models are already trained.
cues.zh: 訓練後，再做機制研究。

cues.en: In contrast, the idea of training interpretable models would be to only train models that have architectures and algorithms that we humans can understand.
cues.zh: 相反地，後者只訓練人類能理解架構、演算法的模型。

cues.en: So you can imagine that people who are interested in outcomes are going to go for interpreting trained
cues.zh: 所以，重視結果的人，偏好解釋訓練好的

cues.en: models, whereas people who are interested in the internal workings, especially as it regards to safety, are proponents of training interpretable models.
cues.zh: 模型；重視內部運作、尤其安全的人，支持訓練可解釋模型。

cues.en: Now, the thing is that if the models are trained based on maximizing capability without concern of
cues.zh: 但若只最大化能力，不管

cues.en: how or why they work, then AI safety is just much, much harder.
cues.zh: 如何、為何運作，安全就難得多。

cues.en: It would be like taking a newly developed medicine to try to treat some medical condition, but nobody has any idea how that medicine actually works.
cues.zh: 像用新藥治病，卻沒人知道作用機制。

cues.en: So it might work really well, but without knowing the mechanism, you don't know what are the potential side effects or safety or efficacies.
cues.zh: 可能很有效，但不知機制，就不知道潛在副作用、安全、效力。

cues.en: In contrast, if we would only use models that are interpretable from the moment they start being trained,
cues.zh: 相反，若只用從開始訓練就可解釋的模型，

cues.en: then humans would be in control and would understand the full dynamics and decision making processes inside the model.
cues.zh: 人類就能控制、理解完整動態與決策。

cues.en: And maybe, perhaps this word guaranteed is too strong here because nothing is really guaranteed in life.
cues.zh: 也許 guaranteed，保證，太強，人生沒什麼絕對。

cues.en: But there would certainly be a lot more safety built in right from the start.
cues.zh: 但一開始就會內建更多安全性。

cues.en: If an AI company is training to maximize capabilities and commercial value, then there's really no
cues.zh: 若公司追求能力、商業價值，

cues.en: self-imposed limits on model growth, only practical limits by data availability and compute power.
cues.zh: 模型成長沒有自設限制，只受資料、算力等實務限制。

cues.en: On the other hand, if we limit ourselves to developing models that we know we can interpret and control,
cues.zh: 但若只開發能解釋、控制的模型，

cues.en: then the growth and development of the models is limited by our assessments of safety and risk.
cues.zh: 成長就受安全、風險評估限制。

cues.en: Well, based on this list, I think you can probably guess where the current reality is.
cues.zh: 看清單，應該猜到現實偏哪一邊。

cues.en: The thing is that, for better or worse, most businesses and private consumers of AI are more interested
cues.zh: 不管好壞，多數企業與私人消費者，

cues.en: in having powerful and capable AI systems and just not so interested in interpretability.
cues.zh: 更要強大能力，沒那麼關心可解釋性。

cues.en: Honestly, safety guarantees are the kind of thing that people tend to talk about a lot more than they're willing to spend money or time or resources on.
cues.zh: 老實說，談安全保證，通常比真的願意花錢、時間、資源還多。

cues.en: So in practice, the concept of training interpretable models is important to know about because it's discussed in the field.
cues.zh: 所以，訓練可解釋模型，是領域討論的重要概念。

cues.en: but the reality is that it's unlikely that developing interpretable models will be as commercially attractive
cues.zh: 但現實是，商業吸引力可能不及

cues.en: as developing capable, but more mysterious and complex models.
cues.zh: 更強大、卻神祕複雜的模型。

cues.en: The next distinction is between bottom up and top down mech interp.
cues.zh: 再來是由下而上、由上而下。

cues.en: The idea of bottom up analyses is to start with the lowest level of information that we can access in the model, which are the weights and the activations.
cues.zh: 前者，從最低層、可存取的權重與啟用開始。

cues.en: And then we use those atoms, so to speak, as building blocks to try to understand and explain how the model generates its final outputs.
cues.zh: 把它們當原子、積木，理解、解釋最終輸出。

cues.en: Now, most of mechanistic interpretability and most of what you will learn in the rest of this course is focused on a bottom up approach.
cues.zh: 多數機制研究，以及本課後面，都是由下而上。

cues.en: On the other hand, this kind of reductionist approach is criticized for being too low level, possibly
cues.zh: 但這種還原方式，被批評太低階，可能

cues.en: missing the actual mechanisms of emergence in language models.
cues.zh: 漏掉語言模型真正的湧現機制。

cues.en: Bottom up approaches are also difficult to scale up, from small toy models to very large commercial
cues.zh: 也難從小玩具模型擴展到大型商用

cues.en: models, and a lot of the activations inside language models just don't seem to be really crucial for processing a given token.
cues.zh: 模型；很多啟用，似乎對某詞元處理不太關鍵。

cues.en: So it's just really challenging to do this kind of work because of the sheer number of neurons inside a language model.
cues.zh: 神經元數太多，真的很難。

cues.en: I'll have more to say about this in the next video on general criticisms of mech Interp.
cues.zh: 下一支一般批評會再談。

cues.en: Then we have the top down approach, which starts from the other side.
cues.zh: 由上而下，從另一端開始。

cues.en: So first you pick a behavior that the model exhibits, and then you try to identify some spatial pattern
cues.zh: 先選模型展現的行為，再找模型中

cues.en: or circuits in the model that are activated when the model exhibits a certain behavior.
cues.zh: 發生該行為時啟動的空間模式、迴路。

cues.en: We can also call this like a psychological approach because we're starting from a behavior and then trying to identify a mechanism.
cues.zh: 也能叫心理學方法，從行為找機制。

cues.en: This approach also has some issues, including the risk of statistical false alarms, which are also called type one errors.
cues.zh: 也有問題，包括統計誤報，第一類錯誤。

cues.en: This approach also suffers a bit from post-hoc non-mechanistic like kind of hand-wavy interpretations,
cues.zh: 還容易事後做非機制、模糊解釋，

cues.en: and it can be difficult to establish causality relative to the bottom up approach.
cues.zh: 相較由下而上，因果關係更難確立。

cues.en: Now, keep in mind that this distinction between bottom up and top down, it's not really as discretized as I'm presenting it in this slide.
cues.zh: 但這區分，沒有投影片看起來那麼離散。

cues.en: A lot of actual research has a little bit of top down and a little bit of bottom up, and both approaches are useful and should be integrated in real research.
cues.zh: 很多研究兩者都有，都有用，應整合。

cues.en: But these are good terms to know about.
cues.zh: 只是值得知道的詞。

cues.en: Now I will tell you about universality.
cues.zh: 接著是普遍性。

cues.en: This is the idea that there are computations or motifs that are learned by all models, including models
cues.zh: 意思是所有模型，包含生圖、文字，

cues.en: that generate images versus text.
cues.zh: 都會學到某些運算、模式。

cues.en: Different architectures, different sizes of LMS, different numbers of parameters, different data sets for training, and so on.
cues.zh: 不論架構、大小、參數量、訓練資料等等。

cues.en: So if a certain finding in MacIntyre is universal, then it would mean that something you discovered
cues.zh: 某發現若具普遍性，就代表

cues.en: in GPT two also exists in Bert and GPT four and in Claude, and all of the language models.
cues.zh: GPT-2 發現的，也存在 BERT、GPT-4、Claude，所有模型。

cues.en: The assumption of universality is why people in MacIntyre will sometimes explore very simple and very small language models.
cues.zh: 這個假設，是研究者有時探索極小、簡單模型的原因。

cues.en: For example, maybe just an embeddings matrix, maybe also one small transformer block on top.
cues.zh: 例如只有嵌入矩陣，也許加一個小 Transformer。

cues.en: On the other hand, keep in mind that universality is an assumption.
cues.zh: 但記得，普遍性是假設，

cues.en: It's a hope.
cues.zh: 是希望。

cues.en: There's no guarantee that a given mechanism that underlies a particular feature of text generation in
cues.zh: 不保證 GPT-2 某個生成特徵的機制，

cues.en: GPT two will also be exactly the same in GPT four.
cues.zh: 在 GPT-4 完全相同。

cues.en: But that is the hope, and that is the motivation for working through analyses in small models before applying them to larger models that are just more difficult to work with.
cues.zh: 這是希望，也是先做小模型、再移到難處理大模型的動機。

cues.en: The lecture so far is by no means a complete set of terms and concepts in mech interp.
cues.zh: 到目前，不是完整的術語概念集合。

cues.en: I'm not going to discuss all the words in this slide.
cues.zh: 不會逐一說明這張所有詞。

cues.en: Most of them you will learn later in the course, and you'll also learn other concepts from other sources that discuss different kinds of analyses in this field.
cues.zh: 大多後面會學，也會在其他分析資料中遇到。

cues.en: So that's it for the terms for now.
cues.zh: 術語先到這裡。

cues.en: In the next lecture, I will give an overview of some general criticisms of the field.
cues.zh: 下一堂概覽一般批評，

cues.en: And then we will be ready to dive into the technical parts.
cues.zh: 再進技術部分。
